dedupe_keys.name: gridlab d agent based power distribution system simulator pnnl battelle

description: GridLAB-D is a power distribution system simulator developed at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, with copyright held by Battelle Memorial Institute. The documentation, read on 2026-09-26, covers built-in distribution models, unbalanced power flow with a Newton-Raphson solver, lines, transformers, regulators, capacitors, fuses, reclosers, switches and substations, reliability and restoration modules, climate inputs, generators, inverters, solar panels, wind turbines, batteries, and residential house models with thermal parameters, water heaters, EV chargers and appliance loads, plus recorders, players, checkpoints and co-simulation with HELICS and EnergyPlus. It is built from source with CMake and a C++ compiler, and Python bindings named gridlabd appeared on PyPI in September 2026 (version 6.0.0a1, Python 3.10 or newer); the wiki lists earlier releases up to 4.3 with Windows and Linux builds. The GridLAB-D licence, version 5.3 of October 2024, allows free use, modification and redistribution with notices retained. Coverage is generic: users model any distribution feeder. Caveats: the Python release is an alpha, and older wiki pages are dated. Simulation uses are network flow, agent-based load behaviour, outage and restoration resilience studies of distribution grids. Related records: data-ieee-pes-distribution-test-feeders supplies standard feeders.
